additional_info.subject: RE: ID0422741-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R3 313057296006]Didn't get RFID access CRM:02681000146
additional_info.body:
Hi Liz Hatton,
Thank you for the update. Please let us know the outcome of the testing once it’s completed, as your feedback will help us proceed with closure.
To clarify, if we need RFID operational on a charger do we need to log a ticket to turn it on, I thought this function could be activated by OCPP?
>> Yes, to have the RFID reader operational on the charger, you will need to log a ticket first. Activating the RFID reader typically requires enabling it on the charger side, which cannot always be done via OCPP alone. Once the reader is activated by our support team, you can then configure and manage RFID functionality through your OCPP backend.
Best Regards,
Sominath Nagalgaon
eMobility Support Team
Please do not change the subject line with replying back to this email.

Hi
Sominath
We are still having issues with the RFID , it looks like it is related to a mismatch on the security profile of the charger and CPO.
Could you change the CPO URL to the below please and also give us some advice as to which security option we should use
OCPP address is -  wss://cpc.novachargehub.co.nz:443/novaenergy
The security options we have are:
0.No Authentication (this is what we had it on and it was rejected by the charger)
1.Unsecured Transport with basic authentication (plain-text authentication)
2. TLS with basic authentication (encrypted authentication)
Thanks for clarifying the RFID set up, I will keep that in mind if we need to turn it on in the future.
Liz

additional_info.body:
Hey Liz,
For additional clarity, when using wss (websocket secured) and security profile of 1/2, the CPO provides the charger with something to authenticate with, in this case a password.
The charger then uses this password for authentication when it connects to the backend.
This is why the charger needs to know the password, otherwise it is not granted access.
Thanks,
